$comment: Real jobs: tasks a person does with this app, each with an outcome a check can observe. Keyed by job id so scripts/merge-json merges two PRs that add different jobs. scripts/jobs check validates every field; jobs.md beside this file is generated from it on dev (scripts/jobs render), never edited. The fields and the done rule: docs/factory/packets.md, Jobs.

RJ-X01.job: Privacy: open, edit and export in every app.
RJ-X01.outcome: No socket opens (lsof shows none); the only network use is Check for Updates, and only when allowed.
RJ-X01.needs_note: none: a network lint and a socket probe are not in the plan
RJ-X01.trap: Blueprint updater checks daily by default; a URLSession call slips into a model

RJ-X02.job: Privacy: Photo File > Export with no metadata strips GPS, serial, MakerNote and IPTC; orientation stays right.
RJ-X02.outcome: The exported JPEG has no GPS, BodySerialNumber, MakerNote or IPTC tags, and its pixels are upright.
RJ-X02.trap: No test holds it; a 'keep' option built on CGImageDestinationAddImageFromSource would copy everything

RJ-X03.job: Privacy: Library export with location off leaves no GPS in the JPEG, the HEIC or the XMP sidecar.
RJ-X03.outcome: No GPS tags in the exported JPEG, the HEIC or the XMP sidecar.
RJ-X03.needs_note: S11 (the metadata option); library/export-pack adds the row
RJ-X03.trap: Sidecar carries xmp:CreateDate and GPS beside a clean file

RJ-X04.job: Privacy: Halo movies, Flare and Design rasters carry no user name, path or host in their metadata.
RJ-X04.outcome: No user name, home path or host name in any metadata of the movies or rasters.
RJ-X04.trap: AVAsset or PNG text chunks pick up a path; untested

RJ-X05.job: Privacy: copying out of Photo puts no source metadata on the pasteboard.
RJ-X05.outcome: The pasteboard image carries no GPS, serial or MakerNote.
RJ-X05.trap: Re-encode via AddImageFromSource from the original would carry GPS

RJ-X06.job: Privacy: saved documents (.ora, .design, .flare, .halo, catalog) hold no absolute paths beyond linked files the person placed.
RJ-X06.outcome: A grep of every saved document finds no $HOME path except the paths of files the person linked.
RJ-X06.trap: Linked placement and recents store home-folder paths; unverified

RJ-X07.job: Privacy: after export, close and quit, no copy of the image is left in temp, caches or a recovery folder.
RJ-X07.outcome: Temp, caches and the recovery folder hold no copy of the image after quit.
RJ-X07.trap: Recovery folders exist by design; cleanup after save is unverified

RJ-X08.job: Security: the app writes only where the person chose and inside its own Application Support.
RJ-X08.outcome: Every file the app writes is in the chosen folder or its own Application Support; a '..' in a name template never leaves the folder.
RJ-X08.needs_note: none (v1 is not sandboxed, suite blueprint)
RJ-X08.trap: A writer resolves '..' in a name template

RJ-X09.job: Install: download the beta, drag to Applications, double-click.
RJ-X09.outcome: It opens without a Gatekeeper block.
RJ-X09.needs_note: none: notarized Developer ID is 'Out' of v1 in the suite blueprint
RJ-X09.trap: Ad-hoc signed bundle is blocked on first open

RJ-X10.job: Update: with no internet, Check for Updates fails quietly and every app keeps working.
RJ-X10.outcome: Offline, Check for Updates fails without a dialog at launch, and every app opens, edits and saves.
RJ-X10.trap: Error dialog on every launch offline

RJ-X11.job: Fidelity: a Photo .ora opens in another OpenRaster editor with its layers.
RJ-X11.outcome: Another OpenRaster editor opens the .ora with the same layers, names and order.
RJ-X11.trap: Masks only in Photo's private folder; untested elsewhere

RJ-X12.job: Fidelity: a PSD test matrix (groups, masks, text, adjustments, 16-bit) opens with a named list of anything dropped.
RJ-X12.outcome: Each matrix file opens, and anything dropped is named in a list before the person goes on.

RJ-X13.job: Fidelity: an SVG exported from Design re-opens in Design, Flare and Halo within 1% pixel difference.
RJ-X13.outcome: The SVG re-opened in Design, Flare and Halo is within 1% pixel difference of the original.
RJ-X13.trap: Text, gradients or shadows lost on the way back

RJ-X14.job: Fidelity: copy vectors in Design and paste into Flare or Halo as editable shapes.
RJ-X14.outcome: The paste arrives as editable vector shapes with the same colours, not a bitmap.

RJ-X15.job: Fidelity: open a JPEG and export it unchanged at quality 90.

RJ-X16.job: Fidelity: an upright portrait phone photo is upright in every app and in every export.
RJ-X16.outcome: Every app shows the portrait upright, and every export is upright with or without metadata.
RJ-X16.trap: Stripping metadata drops the orientation tag on a raw copy

RJ-X17.job: Large: an 8K (7680×4320) photo opens under 3 s, brush p95 under 16 ms, exports under 5 s.
RJ-X17.outcome: Open under 3 s, brush p95 under 16 ms, export under 5 s.

RJ-X18.job: Large: a 100 MP photo opens, crops and exports with memory under budget.
RJ-X18.outcome: The 100 MP photo opens, crops and exports with peak memory under the gate's budget.

RJ-X19.job: Large: 200 brush strokes on an 8K canvas keep memory flat (undo stores tiles).
RJ-X19.outcome: Memory after 200 strokes is within the gate's budget of memory after the first.

RJ-X20.job: Access: do the Instagram crop (RJ-P01) with VoiceOver only.
RJ-X20.outcome: Every control is announced with a name.

RJ-X21.job: Access: do one core job per app with the keyboard only.
RJ-X21.outcome: Each app's core job finishes with no mouse event.
RJ-X21.needs_note: none (a keyboard path is claimed, not job-tested)
RJ-X21.trap: A canvas tool reachable only by mouse

RJ-X22.job: Access: Reduce Motion and Increase Contrast are respected in the chrome.
RJ-X22.outcome: With Reduce Motion on, the chrome doesn't animate; with Increase Contrast on, it draws its higher-contrast look.

RJ-X23.job: Access: flags and labels never rely on colour alone.
RJ-X23.outcome: Every flag and label shows a shape or text as well as its colour.
RJ-X23.trap: Colour dots with no shape or text

RJ-X24.job: Crash: kill -9 each app mid-edit; relaunch restores within one autosave interval.
RJ-X24.outcome: Each app relaunches with an offer to restore that loses no more than one autosave interval.
RJ-X24.trap: Design, Halo and Library lose work today

RJ-X25.job: Undo: save, undo five steps, redo; the file and the canvas agree.
RJ-X25.outcome: After save, undo 5, redo 5, the canvas matches the saved file.

RJ-X26.job: Crash: a full disk while saving keeps the original intact and says why.
RJ-X26.outcome: The original file is byte-for-byte intact and the error names the full disk.
RJ-X26.trap: Non-atomic write truncates the file; unverified

RJ-X27.job: Crash: a truncated or corrupt file opens with a named error, no crash.
RJ-X27.outcome: Each app shows a named error for the damaged file and keeps running.

RJ-X28.job: Suite: double-click a .design, .ora, .flare or .halo in Finder; the right app opens it.
RJ-X28.outcome: Each document type opens in its own app.
RJ-X28.trap: Opens in the launcher or the wrong app

RJ-X29.job: Suite: send a Library photo to Photo and back; rating and original kept.
RJ-X29.outcome: The photo comes back with its rating, and the original file is unchanged.

RJ-X30.job: Give a shape a three-stop linear gradient at 45 degrees by commands alone, drag its middle stop with 120 moves, then undo once.
RJ-X30.outcome: The saved document holds stops at 0, 0.5 and 1 on a 45-degree line through the shape's centre, and after the drag and one undo the middle stop is back at 0.5.
RJ-X30.trap: The 120 moves land as 120 undo steps, or the angle is saved in radians

RJ-X31.job: Make 30 edits by command, jump back 10 steps in the history with one command, then make one more edit.
RJ-X31.outcome: The jump lands on step 20 without recording a step, the document is the state after edit 20, and the new edit replaces the 10 undone steps.
RJ-X31.trap: The jump records a step of its own, or the undone steps survive the new edit

RJ-X32.job: Rotate a shape 15 degrees with one 60-sample drag by commands, flip it, then undo once.
RJ-X32.outcome: The saved shape reads 15 degrees with its position unchanged after the undo of the flip, and a second undo reads 0: the drag was one step.
RJ-X32.trap: The drag lands as 60 undo steps, the turn saves in radians, or the flip moves the shape

RJ-X33.job: Read the colour under three points by command: over a red shape on top of another, in a gradient's middle, and on empty canvas.
RJ-X33.outcome: The overlap reads the top shape's red, the gradient reads its 50% mix within 1 per channel, and empty canvas reads null.
RJ-X33.trap: The sample reads the selected or lower shape

RJ-X34.job: Draw a five-point star by command, try a two-sided polygon, then undo.
RJ-X34.outcome: The star is saved with its kind, points and inner ratio; the polygon is refused with "A polygon needs 3 to 64 sides." and adds nothing; one undo removes the star.
RJ-X34.trap: An out-of-range count is silently clamped, or the star saves as a flat path

RJ-X35.job: Add a 4 pt stroke by command, make it dashed, scrub its trim end to 50% with 60 samples, then undo once.
RJ-X35.outcome: Before the undo the stroke reads dash [16, 8] and trim end 0.5; after it there is no trim: the scrub was one step.
RJ-X35.trap: The dash pattern ignores the width, or the trim saves as a percentage

RJ-X36.job: Put a 3:1 picture into a square box by commands alone, pan it inside the crop with 30 moves, then undo once.
RJ-X36.outcome: The saved document's picture draws 900 x 300 inside the 300 x 300 box (its 3:1 aspect kept, cropped by the box), and after the pan and one undo its focus is back at the centre.
RJ-X36.trap: The picture stretches to fill the square, or the 30 moves land as 30 undo steps

RJ-X41.job: Warm a picture by commands alone: set temperature in 120 drag steps, set shadows, then undo once.
RJ-X41.outcome: After the undo shadows is 0 and temperature 35; the saved tone has only the temperature key; vibrance is refused with its waiting reason.
RJ-X41.trap: 120 steps land as 120 undo steps, or vibrance is accepted while it can't render

RJ-X42.job: Export a 4:5 artwork as JPEG at exactly 1080x1350 by commands alone, then at a long edge of 2048.
RJ-X42.outcome: The first file is exactly 1080x1350, 1080x1351 without stretch is refused with its sentence, the long-edge file is 1638x2048.
RJ-X42.trap: A 2x scale applied on top (2160x2700), off-by-one rounding, or a squashed image

RJ-X43.job: Drop another app's document, an image and an unknown file on an app by commands alone, then list Open Recent.
RJ-X43.outcome: The other app's document and the image are handed to the apps that read them, the unknown file is refused with its sentence, and Open Recent lists only this app's files.
RJ-X43.trap: Another app's document opens here as an import, an unreadable file is silently ignored, or Open Recent lists every app's files

RJ-X37.job: Draw a closed four-point path with one smooth point by commands alone, drag the smooth point's out handle with 120 moves, then undo once.
RJ-X37.outcome: The saved document holds one closed contour of exactly four anchors, the smooth anchor's handles stayed collinear and opposite at every sample, and after one undo its out handle is back where the pen left it.
RJ-X37.trap: Closing adds a duplicate anchor at the start, or the 120 handle moves land as 120 undo steps

RJ-X44.job: Kill Photo, Flare, Design and Halo mid-edit under one support folder, then relaunch each.
RJ-X44.outcome: Each relaunch offers only its own document's edit, Restore brings it back, every app's copy is still on disk, and nothing was written outside the support folder.
RJ-X44.trap: One app's launch deletes another app's recovery copy, or an app ignores -SuiteSupportDir

RJ-X45.job: Set the same exposure and saturation on the same photo in Photo and in Library by command, then export both.
RJ-X45.outcome: The two exports match within 1 level per channel and both differ clearly from the original.
RJ-X45.trap: The same slider gives a different picture in each app (gamma read as its reciprocal, saturation missing, levels units mixed)

RJ-X46.job: Open an Exif-rotated JPEG and a HEIC from the same camera and export each as PNG.
RJ-X46.outcome: Both exports are upright at 3024 x 4032 and match the reference and each other within 3 levels.
RJ-X46.trap: One decode path ignores the orientation or drops the colour profile

RJ-X47.job: Relaunch Library on the same catalog and show the grid.
RJ-X47.outcome: The relaunched grid decodes no unchanged photo, and a photo whose develop settings changed decodes once.
RJ-X47.trap: Every relaunch decodes every photo again, or a developed photo shows its old thumbnail from disk

RJ-X48.job: Make an edit in each of the four editors and close the window.
RJ-X48.outcome: Each asks Save, Don't Save or Cancel with the same words; Cancel keeps the window, Don't Save closes it, a failed save keeps it open.
RJ-X48.trap: An editor closes a dirty window without asking (Halo today), or asks with different words

RJ-X49.job: Sample a 5 x 5 colour at the corner and at the centre of a photo by command.
RJ-X49.outcome: The corner reads the mean of its in-image pixels and the centre the 25-pixel mean, both equal to the kernel's mean.
RJ-X49.trap: Off-image pixels count as black, so the corner reads darker

RJ-X51.job: By commands alone, add a drop shadow to a layer, drag its distance in 120 steps, copy the style onto a second layer, undo once, and export a PNG.
RJ-X51.outcome: After one undo the second layer has no style and the first keeps the last distance; in the PNG the shadow's darkest pixel sits at the shape's edge offset by the distance along the angle (y down) within 1 px, and the shadow is not cut at the layer's bounds.
RJ-X51.trap: The 120 steps land as 120 undo steps, the shadow is clipped at the layer's edge, or the angle is read as radians or with y up

RJ-X50.job: Open a camera RAW file with the afterglow CLI, pull its exposure down one stop, and export it as PNG at full size.
RJ-X50.outcome: The PNG is the RAW file's full 48 x 64 size, upright, within 3 levels of the reference, and its two highlight patches differ by more than 20 levels.
RJ-X50.trap: The export is the embedded preview's size, or the decode went through 8 bits so the clipped highlights come back flat

RJ-X70.job: In Photo, by command: select an ellipse around a face, subtract a lasso over the chin, invert, feather 8 px, fill white, and export.
RJ-X70.outcome: The face centre is unchanged, the notch and surround are white, and the edge ramp from 10% to 90% white is at least 6 px wide.
RJ-X70.trap: Option adds instead of subtracting, the feather is ignored, or Invert selects the whole canvas

RJ-X71.job: In Design, by command: pick a grouped card by its text, move it, enter the group, pick the text and move it alone, then save.
RJ-X71.outcome: After the first move both layers moved 40; after the second only the text moved 10 more.
RJ-X71.trap: The pick lands on the text, so the first move pulls the text out of its card

RJ-X72.job: Copy a red rectangle in Design and paste it into a new image in Photo, then export.
RJ-X72.outcome: Photo gains one 400x200 px layer (2x) whose centre pixel is pure red.
RJ-X72.trap: Photo's Paste is greyed because Design wrote only its own layer type

RJ-X73.job: Paste a screenshot PNG into Design, Flare and Halo and save each.
RJ-X73.outcome: Each file has one new placed-image layer at the pasted pixel size, centred (Halo: in point at the playhead).
RJ-X73.trap: The paste is refused, lands at the top-left corner, or starts at time 0 in Halo

RJ-X74.job: Make a 29.97 fps, 10 s Halo composition with a keyed text layer by command and render a PNG sequence.
RJ-X74.outcome: 300 files, frame 299 timed at 299 x 1001 / 30000 s within 1 microsecond, and drop-frame timecode 00:01:00;02 at frame 1800.
RJ-X74.trap: The composition silently runs at 30, so keys drift a frame on an editor timeline

RJ-X75.job: In Flare and Halo, draw a 200x200 rectangle by command, set its anchor to the centre, key rotation 0 to 360 over 24 frames, and export frames 0 and 12.
RJ-X75.outcome: The opaque pixels' centroid at frame 12 is within 1 px of frame 0's in both apps.
RJ-X75.trap: The spin orbits the canvas's top-left corner, or setting the anchor moves the layer

RJ-X76.job: In Photo, pick the Brush, press size-up twice from 20 px, set opacity 50 by command, stroke on white, and export.
RJ-X76.outcome: The stroke is 30 px tall within 1 and its centre is 50% grey within 3 levels.
RJ-X76.trap: The size steps by 1 so two presses barely change it, or the opacity command sets flow

RJ-X60.job: Apply the built-in high-contrast black and white look to the same photo in Photo and in Library by command, save it as a look named Mine, and export both.
RJ-X60.outcome: Both exports are grey (red, green and blue within 1 level on every pixel) and match each other within 1 level; look.list names Mine after a relaunch.
RJ-X60.trap: The two apps make black and white differently (one desaturates, one mixes the weights), or the saved look is gone after a relaunch

RJ-X61.job: Turn Library's Show Original on and off with the afterglow CLI and read its state back.
RJ-X61.outcome: After view.show-original the json export with contents shown reports original true; toggled twice in one run (a CLI run starts with it off) it reports original false, and the photo's develop values are unchanged both times.
RJ-X61.trap: A toggle an agent can't see or set, so it flips it blind or not at all

RJ-X62.job: Connect an AI assistant to the downloaded app: copy the command from Help > Connect an AI Assistant and run its MCP handshake.
RJ-X62.outcome: The command's path is inside AfterGlow.app, codesign verifies it, and tools/list returns at least one tool for each of the five apps.
RJ-X62.trap: The sheet shows a command that points into the source tree, or an unsigned binary that Gatekeeper stops

RJ-X63.job: In each editor, go to Home with Control-Command-0, open Window > AI Access, run one live command, then close the last window and click the Dock icon.
RJ-X63.outcome: In all five editors Home comes forward, the AI Access window opens, the live command's change shows in the document, and a window exists after the Dock click.
RJ-X63.trap: An editor that strands the tester: no way back to Home, no AI access, or a closed window that never comes back

RJ-X64.job: Open every menu in the launcher and in Flare and click every enabled item once.
RJ-X64.outcome: Every enabled item changes the document, opens a window or sheet, or changes a shown view state; no visible item says it isn't available yet; only Settings is in the placeholder baseline.
RJ-X64.trap: A menu item that looks real and does nothing, reported as a bug on day one

RJ-X65.job: Report a problem from Photo after two Photo crashes, with other apps' and old crash files in the folder.
RJ-X65.outcome: The report lists exactly the two recent Photo crashes, newest first; no home path, user name or host name appears; the run succeeds with the network denied.
RJ-X65.trap: The report leaks the tester's home path or user name, picks up another app's crash, or the app sends it itself

RJ-X66.job: Open each of the five bundled welcome-tour samples headless with its app and export a PNG.
RJ-X66.outcome: Each export has more than 10% non-background pixels, Bounce at frame 15 differs from frame 0, and make-samples --check reports no drift.
RJ-X66.trap: A sample that exists but is stale or empty, so the tour opens a blank canvas
